title: Manipulating Text with jQuery
summary: Shows the two jQuery methods for changing element content: .text() for plain text and .html() for content that includes markup. Both act on every matched element.

concepts.heading: .text()
points: $("h1").text("Bye") replaces the content of the h1 with that string.
Because a jQuery selection covers all matches, $("button").text("Don't Click Me") updates all five buttons in one statement; no loop is needed.
Any HTML tags in the string are treated as literal text, not markup.

concepts.heading: .html()
points: $("h1").html("Bye") parses the string as HTML, so the em tag renders the word in italics.
It is the jQuery equivalent of setting innerHTML in vanilla JavaScript; .text() corresponds roughly to textContent / innerText.
(Extra) Avoid passing untrusted user input to .html(), as it can inject scripts; use .text() for that.

concepts.heading: How jQuery relates to JavaScript
points: Almost everything in jQuery is a method reached with dot notation, such as .css, .addClass, .text.
jQuery is itself written in JavaScript; its methods are wrappers that shorten common tasks, in the same spirit as writing your own functions to cut repetition.
Understanding vanilla JavaScript first makes jQuery understandable rather than magic.

pitfalls: .text() will show tags literally, e.g. an em tag appears as visible characters.
Calling .text(value) with an argument is a setter; with no argument it returns the current text.

gaps_and_ideas: Could be part of one 'jQuery content & attributes' lesson with tasks: change heading text, make it italic with html(), change all five buttons, then read text back with no argument. Demo: input box feeding .text vs .html to show the difference.
